transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Verdant CTO), Eric Wang (Verdant SRE), Monique Lee (Verdant Product Ops)

Summary:
- Follow-up on Verdant production incident on 2026-08-24 where a spike in tail latency caused degraded UX for realtime insights.
- Discussed temporary mitigations, permanent fixes, deployment PR timeline, and next steps for benchmarking and SOC2/infra artifacts.
- Agreed next steps and owners for RCA, staging validation, and performance tests.

Topics:
- Root cause: autoscaler / pod churn interacting with KV cache eviction and long cold starts for model shards.
- Short-term mitigations: increase min-replicas, sticky routing to warm cache, rollback to previous model variant.
- Long-term fixes: autoscaler fix + safer cache eviction strategy, controlled rollout automation, and improved observability (per-request cache/miss metrics).
- Business impact, pricing/contract implications, and prioritization for dedicated capacity.

Action items (captured in metadata above): see action_items field.

Transcript:
[15:00] Jamie Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you see my screen?
[15:03] Alicia Gomez: Yep, can see, thanks.
[15:05] Jamie Patel: Cool. This is just a follow-up to the incident postmortem we circulated. Ravi's got the technical deep-dive for the root cause and the remediation plan. We'll keep it pretty focused so we can get to the next steps.
[15:15] Ravi Menon: Right. So quick recap — on 8/24 we saw a coordinated spike in traffic from a scheduled ETL job plus a customer-facing query burst. Our autoscaler reacted by scaling down earlier than expected because of a bug in the scale-down cooldown logic, which caused pod thrash. When the pods came back up, the KV cache wasn't warm because of a cache eviction pattern tied to sequence length distribution, so cold starts for some model shards were on the order of multiple seconds. That inflated tail latency and some requests timed out in Verdant's client.
[15:25] Eric Wang: Just to be clear, when you say "KV cash" for the cache, do you mean the prefix cache in the serving runtime? Because our traces show sustained prefix miss rate for a 9-minute window.
[15:28] Ravi Menon: Yeah, sorry, prefix cache — the KV cache. The miss rate went from 2% to about 28% during the event window. We also saw the kernel selection fallback take a slightly different path for quantized shards which added a few hundred ms.
[15:35] Monique Lee: Can you explain why rollback wasn't faster? Our folks saw the app switch to a lower-capacity variant and it took like 18 minutes to recover.
[15:40] Jamie Patel: Two reasons — the canary policy we had didn't detect the particular latency regression because it was focused on median latency, not tail. And also our automated fallback to the hosted model variant required a compatible checkpoint; there was a mismatch in model pinning in the deployment config. We should have explicit fallback pins.
[15:46] Ravi Menon: We're adding a tail latency probe to the canary checks and a separate policy for tail SLOs. Also adjusting the autoscaler cooldown window to be more conservative during known batch windows.
[15:52] Alicia Gomez: On the business side — the outage affected 5% of user queries in the analytics portal and about 2 minutes of the dashboard refreshes were showstoppers. We need to quantify cost impact; Monique, can you keep a tally on customer escalations?
[15:57] Monique Lee: Yep, I have a list. Already notified CS.
[16:00] Eric Wang: One technical ask — can you share the request-level logs and trace ids for the high-latency requests? We want to correlate with our Apdex and SLAs.
[16:04] Ravi Menon: Absolutely. I'll drop a bucket of traces and the request IDs; we'll sanitize PII.
[16:08] Jamie Patel: On the mitigation timeline, high priority items we pushed to prod last week were: fix autoscaler cooldown logic (hotfix v2.1.3), increase min-replicas for Verdant's service from 2 to 4 during business hours, and added sticky routing to reduce cold cache churn.
[16:16] Alicia Gomez: We noticed improvement but still saw occasional 200-300ms spikes on tails. Is that expected?
[16:19] Ravi Menon: Yes, some residual spikes are expected until we deploy the safer eviction algorithm. The current sticky routing reduces misses but doesn't eliminate them when there's a large cohort of unique prefixes.
[16:25] Eric Wang: For the eviction algorithm — what's the plan? LRU + frequency threshold?
[16:28] Ravi Menon: We're prototyping a hybrid TTL + LFU weighting that prefers keeping recently used KV entries for active sessions. Also we want to tag long-lived sessions so the cache prioritizes those prefixes.
[16:35] Monique Lee: Does this change require a restart or will it be hot-deployable? We can't afford more churn.
[16:38] Ravi Menon: Goal is hot-deployable. It's a runtime switch to the eviction policy and a config flag; we'll validate in staging. However the rollout needs staged traffic shifting to avoid large-scale misses.
[16:44] Alicia Gomez: On the security/compliance ask — our legal team is requesting the audit log snippets showing who triggered the rollback and the deployment diffs.
[16:49] Jamie Patel: We'll provide the deployment audit and the operator actions. Ravi, can you pull together the KMS logs and any config change IDs?
[16:52] Ravi Menon: Yep — KMS integration is intact; no key exposure. I'll export the audit stream for the 8/24 timeframe.
[16:57] Eric Wang: Also, we want to discuss Dedicated vs Hosted — given this incident, our execs are asking if dedicated capacity would prevent this class of outage. Thoughts?
[17:01] Jamie Patel: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives you predictable min capacity, but it doesn't remove software bugs like the autoscaler cooldown. It does, however, reduce contention on shared cache and can make rollbacks more predictable because you control the pool. We'll send a comparative analysis for your workload patterns.
[17:08] Monique Lee: Any immediate options that are cheaper than full dedicated?
[17:10] Jamie Patel: Yes — reserved burst capacity + pinned replicas during business hours is an intermediate step. Also configuring a higher min-replicas and explicit fallback pins for model variants.
[17:15] Alicia Gomez: About the SLA credit conversation, we might need to open that if the customer impact threshold is met. Jamie, can you prepare the incident impact numbers for our billing team?
[17:20] Jamie Patel: Yep, I'll prepare a summary of affected request volume and estimated cost impact; we'll include it with the RCA.
[17:24] Ravi Menon: One more technical note — we found a gap in our observability: per-request cache miss metrics weren't tagged with model shard id which made root cause a bit slower to find. We'll add shard-level tagging and increase retention for those metrics for 30 days around rollouts.
[17:30] Eric Wang: Perfect. For the performance benchmark session, we'd like Redwood to run a replay with our synthetic traffic pattern (burst + ETL overlap). We'll provide a dataset and credentials.
[17:33] Jamie Patel: Great, once we have the dataset we'll schedule the 1.5 hour bench and run both hosted vs dedicated profiles.
[17:38] Monique Lee: Quick Q — do you have an updated checklist for the canary rollout? Our ops prefer a checklist we can follow.
[17:41] Ravi Menon: We do. I'll attach the canary checklist to the RCA email: includes tail probes, shard-level metrics, fallback pins, rollback playbook, and contact matrix.
[17:46] Alicia Gomez: Any blocker on the RCA itself? We need that by early next week.
[17:49] Jamie Patel: We're targeting EOD Friday for the full RCA with timeline, root cause detail, and the mitigation plan. That's 2026-09-03.
[17:53] Eric Wang: Sounds good. One last thing — competitors' tooling was mentioned by our infra folks: Mistral Cloud claims autorecovery on cold-cache events, do you have any notes on that?
[17:57] Ravi Menon: Some vendors bake in warmer fallback layers and heavier per-request caching, but that often comes with increased cost. We'll include a short competitor note with the RCA.
[18:00] Jamie Patel: Alright, thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps: Redwood will send RCA (Jamie/Ravi), Ravi will export audit/KMS logs, Eric will send traces and synthetic dataset, Jamie will share pricing/impact and schedule the bench. We'll reconvene after the bench to decide on dedicated or reserved pool.
[18:06] Alicia Gomez: Thanks all.
[18:06] Meeting ends.
